Header: Pterolophia annulata Chevr Sinhala – Kandan vidina kuruminiya; Tamil – Milaku kodi thulaippan

Prevention: Remove weeds about 2 feet around the pepper vine in field
Slash all weeds in rest of the field
Cut and remove all ground runners and lower side branches that touch the ground
Monitoring: Look for damage symptoms: withering or yellowing of plant parts or the whole vine. small, round holes on the stem
Direct Control: Remove and burn infested plant part or whole plants showing damage symptoms and/ or holes caused by the pest
Rate of dilution – 5 ml / 10 lit. of water.
Rate of dilution – 10 ml / 10 lit. of water
Restrictions: Apply insecticide to the infected vines and surround healthy vines after removing and burning the damaged parts / vines.
Always wear personal protective equipment while handling pesticides.
Read manufacturer’s instructions carefully before handling pesticides.
Do not eat, drink or smoke while spraying pesticides
Toxic to aquatic organisms, bees, certain birds and reptiles.
Toxic to predatory mites, flower bugs, parasitoids, ladybird beetles and moderately toxic to lacewings.
